thread:
diego: hey team — getting an escalation from a large customer (acct: acme-inc). They see 5xxs from our inference API when they should be getting 429s for rate limits. Customer has a ton of traffic but we should still return 4xx. can we triage? :exclamation:

nadia: customer called in, very upset. they say it started ~30m ago, intermittent 500s across multiple endpoints, e.g., /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. they captured a few request IDs and responses. sharing below.

oncall-bot: alert: 3xx error-rate increase for hosted-api in us-west-2 (rate-limit errors returning 5xx). alert id: ALRT-2026-03-15-15:12

maya: putting on incident priority. pinging runtime and api teams. I’ll grab traces from gateway and rate-orch.

sven: looking. initial hypothesis: quota/rate-limiter service returning a 500 due to upstream timeout, gateway currently maps quota errors to 5xx instead of 4xx in this path. sending logs now.

diego: customer-sent example (sanitized):
```bash
curl -i -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \ 
  -H 'X-Request-ID: r-0a7f3c' \ 
  -d '{"model":"open-llm-13b","prompt":"hello"}'
```
response body they got:
```json
{"error":{"message":"internal server error","code":500,"request_id":"r-0a7f3c"}}
```
customer also attached api-gateway logs showing upstream status 504 from quota-checker: `upstream_status=504` and then the gateway returned 500.

priya: confirmed - gateway trace shows request routed to `rate-orch-eu` mistakenly (region mismatch) due to header-based routing rule change from earlier deploy. that `rate-orch-eu` cluster was experiencing high latencies to its backing redis shards and timing out. the gateway treats upstream 5xx/504 as unknown error and bubbles 500.

deploy-bot: deploy: rate-orch-service v3.14.2 -> v3.15.0 deployed by @priya at 2026-03-15T14:55:12Z to us-west-2 (canary->prod).

maya: ok, looks like a misroute to a degraded cluster plus missing mapping logic. immediate mitigation options:
- route traffic away from `rate-orch-eu` to healthy pool
- change gateway mapping so quota-check failures map to 429 when appropriate, even on dependency timeouts (short term)
- rollback the v3.15.0 deploy if routing rollback isn't quick

sven: I can flip a routing rule to prefer `rate-orch-west` and add a temporary circuit-breaker to fail-fast to 429 for quota-check timeouts. will need a quick config push to the gateway.

priya: prepping config patch now. patch will: 1) prefer local West cluster for us-west traffic, 2) add a mapping: when quota-check returns 5xx or times out, interpret it as QUOTA_UNAVAILABLE and respond 429 to callers instead of 500 (with header X-Quota-Status: degraded). also adding a telemetry tag so we can distinguish true 5xx vs mapped-429s.

sven: rollout plan: push gateway config to canary (5% traffic), verify customer requests -> 429 instead of 500, then promote to 50% and 100% if green. will also drain traffic from `rate-orch-eu` for now.

maya: go for canary. I’ll monitor traces and latency dashboards.

[~10m later]

priya: pushed canary config. sample test (local repro):
```bash
# simulate quota dependency timeout
curl -i -X POST \"https://canary.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -H 'Authorization: Bearer test' -H 'X-Request-ID: r-test1' -d '{"model":"m","prompt":"x"}'
```
observed response:
```json
{"error":{"message":"rate limit pending: quota service unavailable, try again","code":429,"request_id":"r-test1","quota_status":"degraded"}}
```

sven: canary looks good. metrics: 500s from quota flow dropped from 18/min -> 2/min on canary (those 2 are unrelated). promoting to 50%.

oncall-bot: deploy: gateway-config v2026-03-15-214 -> v2026-03-15-215 canary=5% by priy a

[~20m later]

priya: promoted to 100%. `rate-orch-eu` has been drained and its autoscaler set to 0 for now.

diego: customer confirmed they now receive 429s instead of 500s for their throttle bursts. they acepted an interim explanation and will be monitoring. :relieved:

nadia: I emailed the account team and the customer. summarized root cause and interim mitigation, promised a follow-up RCA.

maya: quick post-incident notes: root cause = header-routing change in prior deploy + overloaded `rate-orch-eu` causing dependency timeouts -> gateway mapping treated upstream timeout as 500 instead of a quota fallthrough. why it returned 500: missing explicit gateway mapping for QUOTA upstream timeouts.

action items (owner):
- eng-runtime / priya: add explicit mapping logic so quota-check timeouts consistently return 429 and include `quota_status` header (PR by EOD) (owner: priya)
- eng-sre / maya: add synthetic tests to detect cluster routing mismatches and failover (owner: maya)
- infra / sven: add circuit-breaker + local warm cache in gateway to reduce dependency calls during spikes (owner: sven)
- product / nadia: customer comms and SLA credit evaluation (owner: nadia)
- postmortem writeup on confluence and add to monthly ops review (owner: diego)

sven: I'll also add an alert: if gateway observes >5% of quota failures coming back as 5xx across a 5m window, fire P0.

diego: thanks all. leaving this open for the RCA doc. moving to monitoring/watch for the next 24h. :eyes:
